title: Less admin. More human.
tagline: Four copy-and-paste AI prompts that clear the busywork, so you can show up for the conversations that actually matter.

cover_footer.lead: Built for brains with 14 tabs open.
cover_footer.aside: Skim it. Grab a prompt. Close the tab.

how_it_works.text: the box into ChatGPT, Claude or any AI chat.
every yellow part for your own details.
the answer before you use any of it.

safety_note: No accounts to connect. For work, use an AI tool your company approves and only share what you are allowed to share. Every example in this guide is made up, and AI still gets details wrong.

prompts.title: Walk in with better questions.
prompts.trigger: I have a recruiter call coming up.
prompts.use_when: A recruiter call is coming up and you have way too many tabs open.
prompts.have_ready: The job post + 5 facts about your work
prompts.prompt:
Help me prep for a recruiter call. Use only what I paste below.

Give me:
1. Five specific questions about the role, the team and how the work actually runs.
2. Three moments from my background worth bringing up, and why each one fits.
3. Anything important the job post leaves unclear.

Do not invent experience or script my answers. Keep it to one page.

JOB POST: {{job_post}}
MY BACKGROUND: {{background}}

example.input: A Senior Software Engineer, GenAI role that mentions LLM evals and a hybrid schedule. Your background includes Python APIs and an internal RAG prototype.
example.output: “How many days a week would I be in the office, and is that set or flexible?”

next_steps: Circle the 2 or 3 questions you actually care about
Pick one real story for each example
Say it your way on the call. No script.

prompts.title: Before you hire, get clear on the work.
prompts.trigger: Our job brief turned into a wish list.
prompts.use_when: The brief now lists everything the team might ever need.
prompts.have_ready: Your rough hiring notes, messy is fine
prompts.prompt:
Turn these rough hiring notes into a short brief for a sourcer.

Sort it into:
1. What this person must deliver in their first 6 months.
2. Skills that are essential to those outcomes, with a reason for each.
3. Skills they could learn on the job.
4. Three decisions we need to make before the search starts.

Treat your suggestions as proposals, not agreed requirements. Flag anything that contradicts itself. Do not add requirements just because similar job ads list them.

HIRING NOTES: {{notes}}

example.input: “We need a Product Manager for our GenAI assistant. Technical enough to write prompts and read eval results. Pricing experience would be nice. Not sure yet if they report to product or engineering.”
example.output: “Does this PM report to product or engineering? That changes who you are looking for.”

next_steps: Settle the 3 open decisions with your team
Send the shorter brief. Clearer search, clearer pitch.

prompts.title: Find a new place to look.
prompts.cover_label: Find a new place to look
prompts.trigger: My search keeps showing the same people.
prompts.cta: Find a new place to look
prompts.use_when: Every search returns the same profiles. Same work often hides under a different title.
prompts.have_ready: Outcomes, must-haves, titles you already search

example.input: “Ship LLM features to production: retrieval and evals. Must have shipped an LLM feature real users rely on. We search: Machine Learning Engineer.”
example.output_label: One idea it might give you
example.output: Search or backend engineers who built retrieval systems. Check they shipped to production. A weekend RAG demo does not prove it.

next_steps: Try one new title this week
Look for the evidence, not the title
Ask the test question on the first call

prompts.title: Stop rewriting the follow-up.
prompts.trigger: I just got off a call and owe a follow-up.
prompts.cta: Send it while it is fresh
prompts.use_when: You just finished a kickoff, networking call or project chat.
prompts.have_ready: A few rough bullets. That is enough.
prompts.prompt:
Turn these rough notes into a short follow-up I can review and send.

Use three sections: Agreed, Still open, Next steps.
For each next step, include an owner and a deadline only if my notes say so. Otherwise write "to confirm".

Keep maybes separate from commitments. Do not add promises, decisions or dates. Plain, warm language. Under 150 words.

NOTES: {{notes}}

example.input: “Sam sends the AI Engineer brief Friday. Comp still undecided. Maybe ask Lee to join the next call.”
example.output_label: A good draft keeps it straight

next_steps: Check every name, date and promise
Change one line so it sounds like you

prompts.title: Strip the AI tells.
prompts.trigger: This sounds like a robot wrote it.
prompts.use_when: The facts are right but the draft reads like a template.
prompts.prompt:
Edit this so it does not read like AI wrote it. Remove long dashes, filler openers, buzzwords and anything that sounds like a template. Mix short and long sentences. Keep every fact and do not add new ones.

TEXT: {{text}}

example.input: “I hope this finds you well! I’d love to connect and explore how we can leverage synergies.”
example.output: “Hi Sam, good to meet you at the meetup. Want to grab 20 minutes next week to compare notes on hiring?”

next_steps: Make sure nothing new was added

prompts.audience: Bonus · use it on any answer
prompts.title: Teach it your voice.
prompts.trigger: It’s fine, it just doesn’t sound like me.
prompts.blurb: Give it a few things you actually wrote: emails, posts, texts. It picks up your words, your rhythm and your personality, then adapts.
prompts.use_when: You want every draft to sound like you wrote it.
prompts.have_ready: 2 or 3 emails or posts you wrote

fields.label: How I'd describe my style
fields.hint: 3 words, like direct, warm, a bit funny

fields.label: My samples
fields.hint: paste or upload 2 or 3 emails or posts

example.input: Three of your own emails, the words “direct, warm, a bit funny” and a stiff intro email.
example.output: Shorter sentences, your usual sign-off and the kind of line you would actually say. Same facts.

next_steps: Fix any line you would never say
Save your samples in one note for next time

bonus_page.kicker: Bonus · use it on any answer above
bonus_page.title: Make it sound like you.
bonus_page.intro_lead: AI writing has tells, and people notice.
bonus_page.intro: Two quick moves fix most of it.
bonus_page.pro_move: Keep your samples in one note so you can reuse them. Many AI tools also let you save your style once so it applies every time.
last_check: Fix any line you would never say

fixes.text: “The team has no dedicated infrastructure engineer” beats “we are a fast-moving startup.”

fixes.reply: Keep only the three things that change what I do next.
Rewrite this the way I would say it out loud. Shorter sentences.
fixes.note: Want it to sound exactly like you? Use the bonus voice prompt.

closing.title: Try one prompt on one task this week.
closing.text: Then spend the time you get back on what AI cannot do for you: a real conversation, a thoughtful reply, or an actual break.

further_reading: Further reading: Anthropic's prompting best practices at docs.claude.com (checked October 7, 2026). These prompts are starting points and results vary. All examples are made up, not client cases or measured results.
